## Code Review

This pull request introduces a comprehensive and well-structured documentation file for email mailbox operations, covering organization, triage, and various workflows. It also updates the main agent index to include this new document. The new guide is detailed and provides valuable patterns and examples. I've identified a couple of minor issues in the code examples that could be improved for correctness and consistency.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a comprehensive set of email provider configurations as a JSON template and detailed corresponding documentation in a markdown file. The information is well-structured and covers a wide range of providers and technical details. My review identified a minor data quality issue: the verification date for the settings is listed as a future date (`2026-03`) in both files. This appears to be a typo and should be corrected to ensure the information is accurate and trustworthy. Both comments have been retained as they are valid and do not contradict any of the provided rules.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a comprehensive `apple-mail-helper.sh` script to interact with Apple Mail via AppleScript. The implementation covers a wide range of functionalities as described. The code is well-structured, but there are several areas for improvement regarding robustness, security, and maintainability. My review focuses on addressing potential bugs in argument parsing, security vulnerabilities from unescaped variables in AppleScript, and opportunities to reduce code duplication for better long-term maintenance.

Overall, this is a great addition that will be very helpful for users of the agent.

Additionally, I've provided more robust `jq` commands to prevent potential errors when processing API responses for contacts that may have missing data.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a comprehensive email security guide. The document is well-structured and covers critical topics. I've provided a few suggestions to improve the correctness and robustness of the shell script examples, particularly regarding a flawed prompt injection scanning pattern, an inconsistent file extension blocklist, and a bug in base64 encoding that would break JSON creation.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a comprehensive documentation file for an email intelligence agent. The document is well-structured and covers various aspects from model routing to voice mining and FAQ systems. No specific review comments were found that require changes based on the project's established rules.

## Code Review

This pull request adds a comprehensive email security guide. The documentation is well-structured and covers many important topics. However, I've found a few critical and high-severity issues in the provided code examples that could lead to security vulnerabilities if implemented as-is. My review includes suggestions to fix an insecure sender verification method, a credential scanning check that can fail silently, and an incomplete prompt injection scanning workflow. It's crucial that security documentation provides robust and safe examples.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a new, comprehensive guide for email mailbox operations. The document is well-structured, covering key aspects of email management. I have provided a couple of suggestions to improve the clarity of an instruction and to correct a code example to make it more robust.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a sensible improvement by deriving the default `MAX_WORKERS_CAP` from the system's total RAM instead of using a static value. The implementation correctly handles memory detection for both macOS and Linux, with a safe fallback for other operating systems. The logic for calculating and clamping the worker cap is sound. I have one minor suggestion to enhance code clarity.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a comprehensive library of 20 reusable email templates and a manifest for managing common email attachments. The templates are well-structured and cover a variety of communication scenarios with formal and casual variants. The attachment manifest is a good step towards standardizing how attachments are handled.

My review focuses on ensuring the new additions are secure and maintainable. I've identified a potential security vulnerability in the attachment manifest related to path traversal that should be addressed in the agent consuming this file. I've also suggested a minor improvement to one of the email templates for better clarity and consistency.
